reason: Caryopsis is the grass fruit (PO_0009001); 'dark brown' is its colour.

In FNA Eriogonum, the habit dimension 'H × W dm' gives height × width of the plant; the second range is the width, and 3–6 dm = 30–60 cm.

fix: 'open' said of an inflorescence (cyme, panicle, raceme) means lax, with spaced branches and flowers, the opposite of dense or congested. Map it to loose, like 'lax', not to PATO open, which means having an opening.
reason: '± open cymes' describes how loose the inflorescence is, not an opening.
'seed not grooved': negated grooved on seed, right scope.
These are leaflets (petiolules follow); 'glabrous above' = adaxial surface glabrous. Leaf adaxial epidermis covers the leaflet's upper surface.
'apex rounded' on the leaf blade = obtuse (PATO synonym roundish). The 'lower stem leaves' context is lost, but the statement is still true of the taxon.
'suborbicular' = approximately orbicular, as recorded; the lateral sepals are sepals.
'Glumes subequal' = glumes approximately equal in size (FLOPO_0991102 with the 'approximately' qualifier), the agreed reading of 'subequal'.
Pedicels 'with some scattered hairs or glabrous': hairy | glabrous alternatives on the pedicel.

In Sideroxylon the petal has a median segment and basal lateral segments. '(lobed basally)' may mean the median segment is lobed at its base, or refer to the lateral segments, which are said to be vestigial or absent. 'Petal base lobed' is a plausible but uncertain reading.
'leaf blade ... abaxially pubescent' = abaxial lamina epidermis pubescent. 'denser on midrib' is only a further detail.
Follicles are fruits; dark brown.
'slightly spreading or erect' = taxon-level alternatives spreading (degree 'slightly') or erect for the stem position.

fix: Teeth of a calyx (or corolla) are its lobes. Map 'calyx with N teeth' or 'calyx teeth' to calyx lobe (FLOPO_0986005) with the count, not to phyllome lamina tooth, which is a marginal serration of a lamina.
reason: 'calyx with 4-5 teeth' counts calyx lobes (Lycopus); the count is right.

fix: 'N-fid' after 'petals ... apex' in a family with free petals (Caryophyllaceae) describes the cleft tip of each free petal, not lobes of a fused corolla. Corolla lobe is only right for sympetalous corollas. Read '2-fid' as bifid (PATO_0001784) on the petal or its apex.
reason: Cerastium petals are free; the apex of each petal is 2-cleft.
'Rhizome erect or ascending': position alternatives on the rhizome.

fix: 'in N row(s) on each side of X' gives the number of rows, an arrangement of the part (here uniseriate on each side of the costa), not the number of the parts. Do not turn it into a count of the part.
reason: Sori are 'more numerous on acroscopic side'; they are many, set in 1 row each side. Sorus amount = 1 is false. The midrib here is the pinna costa.

fix: Keep 'lateral' / 'dorsal' as the position slot on orchid sepals: only the lateral sepals are adnate to the column foot and form the mentum.

'Stems sparsely pubescent proximally' = the proximal part of the stem is pubescent (the 'sparsely' degree is dropped, which is harmless).
Lower bracts serrate with up to 11 teeth on each side: tooth count ≤11 per side on the bract, with the each-side position.
The spikes are 'oblong in outline'; the spike is the inflorescence.
